name: daily_wr_swing
written: 2026-11-20, before any script was written or any outcome computed
operator: 11/20 'Yes, pre-register A' (Path A from a pasted review: raw daily %R oversold mean reversion in an uptrend, held 1-5 days)
question: On daily bars, does buying a liquid stock that is above its 200-day average when raw Williams %R says oversold, and selling on the snap-back, beat buying other uptrend names over the same days, by enough to pay a realistic cost?
prior_work_not_repeated: rsi2_daily (10/9: RSI-2 < 10 above SMA200, held open->close of ONE day only, as a day-trading picker); daily_horizon #4 one-week losers (11/11: bottom tenth by 5-day return, no trend filter, 5-day hold, FAIL beta-adj -17.9 bp t -1.65); monthly_book R5 one-month reversal (FAIL). None used %R, the SMA200 filter AND an exit on the snap-back. Every intraday %R test failed; this is %R on the timeframe it was designed for.
prior: LOW, about 15%: published daily mean-reversion rules (Connors RSI-2, %R) have weakened since ~2010 and are strongest in index ETFs, not single stocks; one-week losers already failed here.
data: ~/lh_cache/panel.npz on the mini: 2016-01-04..2026-09-25, 6,227 symbols with adjusted o/h/l/c/v, raw close rc and status (active/inactive). Verdict window 2017-01-03..2022-12-30 only, halves split at 2020-01-01, because inactive (delisted) names are present for those years but almost absent for 2023+ (the 10/7 earnings study counted ~21). 2023-01..2026-09 is printed as INFORMATION, never a verdict. The script prints, per year, the count of names that stop trading.
universe: on day t, a name is tradeable when its raw close on t >= $10 and its mean raw dollar volume (rc x v) over the 20 sessions ending t >= $20M, with >= 190 finite closes in the 200 sessions ending t. SPY and every symbol in the SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA-style ETF list the script prints are excluded from the stock test (ETFs are an information line).

signal (decided at the close of t, raw,.trend: C[t] > SMA200[t] (simple mean of the 200 adjusted closes ending t)
signal (decided at the close of t, raw,.wr: %R_N[t] = -100 x (max(H[t-N+1..t]) - C[t]) / (max(H[t-N+1..t]) - min(L[t-N+1..t])); a zero range is no signal

trade.entry: buy at the OPEN of t+1 (no look-ahead: the signal uses t's close)
trade.exit: the first close s >= t+1 with %R_N[s] > -20 OR C[s] > SMA5[s]; sell at the OPEN of s+1. If neither by the close of t+5, sell at the open of t+6 (hold at most 5 sessions)
trade.one position per name: no new entry on a name while its previous trade is open
trade.delisting: a name that stops trading is sold at its last close
trade.clip: per-trade return clipped to [-90%, +300%] (data errors), count printed

cost: money line 30 bp per round trip (the desk measured ~31 bp for market orders at the open; same line as daily_horizon); 10 bp printed as information
control (primary): per trade: the equal-weight mean return of ALL tradeable names on the signal day that are above their SMA200 and NOT oversold on that variant, bought at the same open of t+1 and sold at the same exit open, same clip and delisting rule. Lift = (1+r)/(1+c) - 1 per trade.
controls (information): (a) same-name control: the same name on a random tradeable day within +/-60 sessions with C > SMA200 and %R_N > -50, held the same number of sessions (seed 41); (b) all tradeable names, no trend filter; (c) SPY over the same window.
statistic: per variant, trade-weighted mean lift (bp) and the beta-adjusted residual r - beta x c (beta = OLS of r on c over all of that variant's trades in the half); t clustered by ENTRY WEEK (overlapping holds share weeks).
power: before any mean is read: per variant and half, SE and MDE = 2.8 x SE. A variant whose MDE > 30 bp in either half is UNDERPOWERED, no verdict.

pass (per variant, all required).edge: mean lift > 0 in both halves AND pooled clustered t >= 2.39 (two-sided 5% over 3 variants) AND the beta-adjusted residual's clustered t >= 2.39
pass (per variant, all required).money: mean lift - 30 bp > 0 in BOTH halves
pass (per variant, all required).robust: still > 0 (lift - 30 bp) after dropping the top 1% of trades by lift, and after dropping the best calendar quarter

fail: anything short of pass. No retuning of N, the -90/-20 levels, SMA200/SMA5, the 5-session cap or the entry/exit timing; a changed rule is a new prereg on data that has now been seen.
information_only: entry at the CLOSE of t instead of the next open (the textbook MOC version; mildly optimistic)

RSI2 (operator 11/20 'Yes, add the RSI-2 line'): signal RSI-2 < 10 (Wilder, 2-period, on adjusted closes, >= 20 bars of history) above SMA200; exit on the first close with RSI-2 > 70 OR C > SMA5, else the 5-session cap; same entry, control (uptrend names with RSI-2 >= 10), lift, beta residual and 30 bp line, printed next to the three %R variants; information only, not a fourth hypothesis
exit on %R only, and on SMA5 only
ETF line (SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA and sector SPDRs present in the panel), same rule
a 10-slot equal-weight account after 30 bp vs SPY: yearly return, worst drawdown, Sharpe, over 200 tie-break seeds (median and range)
win %, median hold, share of total from the top 1% of trades
checks: unit test: %R matches a hand computation on a 10-bar series
unit test: the exit fires on the first qualifying close and sells the next open; the 5-session cap sells at t+6's open
null canary: synthetic drift with no edge must not read PASS; a planted +60 bp snap-back must read EDGE
assert >= 100 tradeable names on every entry day
print counts: signals, skipped for open position, clipped, delisted exits
if_pass: result-skeptic review; then a paper swing book is a SEPARATE decision for the operator (the day desk is unchanged)
if_fail: record it; daily %R mean reversion joins one-week losers and RSI-2 daily as closed
pre_run_review: result-skeptic reviews this prereg before any code runs (standing checkpoint)
script: tools/studies/daily_wr_swing.py (to be written after the review)

amended_1.when: 2026-11-20, after the result-skeptic pre-run review (FIX FIRST: 1 blocker, 4 majors, 4 minors), before any script or outcome; the skeptic's power probe printed SEs only
amended_1.B1 verdict window (replaces the 2017-202: no name in the panel stops trading before 2018-06 (last-bar years 2017: 0, 2018: 90, 2019: 217, 2020: 139, 2021: 211, 2022: 142, 2023: 3). Verdict window 2018-07-02..2022-12-30, halves split at 2020-10-01. 2017-01..2018-06 and 2023+ are INFORMATION. The per-year stop count is printed for all names and for names liquid at their last bar.
amended_1.M1 beta-timing (added to EDGE): (a) SPY residual r - beta x SPY over the same open-to-open window, clustered t >= 2.39; (b) vol-matched control: equal-weight of control names in the same trailing 20-day realized-vol quintile at t, mean lift > 0 in both halves; (c) entry-day-weighted mean lift (each entry day counted once) > 0 in both halves. Canary added: a market factor with heterogeneous betas plus a planted index reversal and no stock-specific edge must not read EDGE.
amended_1.M2 clustering: all t statistics and the MDE are clustered by ENTRY CALENDAR MONTH (replaces entry week)
amended_1.M3 power: UNDERPOWERED (MDE > 30 bp) in either half = UNPROVEN, recorded as such, not FAIL and not closed
amended_1.M4 same-name control: drawn only from t+hold+2 .. t+hold+62, C > SMA200, %R_N > -50, same hold length; each control's mean is printed beside the unconditional mean (a random uptrend name-day, same hold); a control far from that mean (|diff| > 2 SE) blocks the verdict
amended_1.m1 ETF line: dropped: none of SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA/sector or leveraged ETFs are in the panel's symbol list; the script prints any ETF-like symbols it finds
amended_1.m2 data hygiene: status is as of today and is never a filter. %R and SMA windows need every bar finite; a NaN bar during a hold exits at the last close before it; a NaN open at t+1 skips the signal (counted)
amended_1.m3 robustness: the TEST_STANDARD veto is the top-1% winsorized mean (lift - 30 bp > 0 in both halves); dropping the top 1% of trades and the best quarter remain as stricter extra vetoes
amended_1.m4 money lines: also print raw net r - 30 bp per half as the TEST_STANDARD PROFITABLE line; the 30 bp-on-lift line stays the money bar
amended_1.RSI2 line (skeptic addendum): the RSI-2 line uses the amended verdict window, SPY residual, vol-matched and entry-day-weighted controls, monthly clusters and the post-trade same-name control, and shares every trade rule (one position per name, delisting exit at the last close, [-90%,+300%] clip, NaN-open skip, NaN-gap exit). Wilder RSI-2: smoothing alpha 1/2 (adjust=False) seeded at the first change, computed only on contiguous finite closes (a NaN gap restarts the seed), >= 20 bars after the seed; avg loss 0 -> RSI 100; avg gain = avg loss = 0 -> no signal. Signals with C[t] >= SMA5[t] (any variant) are counted and printed, not dropped. The RSI-2 line cannot promote, rescue or replace a %R variant; a good RSI-2 number needs its own prereg on a forward window.

result_2026-11-20: WR3 FAIL, WR5 FAIL, WR10 UNDERPOWERED -> UNPROVEN (h2 MDE 36.9 > 30). Verdict window 2018-07..2022, lift vs uptrend-not-oversold names over the same days, bp/trade (h1 / h2, pooled month-clustered t): WR3 -1.5 / +9.1 (t 0.89, n 52,264); WR5 -3.2 / +14.7 (t 1.05, n 41,973); WR10 -3.0 / +27.8 (t 1.73, n 30,390). Money line 30 bp: none close. Raw return ~+31 bp/trade but the control made ~+26 over the same days (market bounce). Win ~64%; top 1% of trades ~half the total. Information: every variant negative or ~0 in h1 (7/2018-9/2020) and positive in h2 (10/2020-2022); pre-2018-07 ~0 (-2.2/-0.7/+1.3); 2023+ +4..+7 bp. %R<=-95 +9/+26 (t 2.0); no SMA200 filter +3/+31 (t 2.4) but raw net30 -12.7; RSI-2<10 +0.7/+20.2 (t 1.3), raw net30 -4.2, 2023+ +15. SMA5-only exit = the full rule (the %R>-20 exit never fired first). 10-slot account after 30 bp: -3% to -17%/yr median, drawdowns -51% to -62%, vs SPY +10.0%/yr. Plain words: daily %R oversold-in-uptrend does not beat simply holding other uptrend names over the same days by anything near its cost; the only positive stretch is late 2020-2022. ai_reports/daily_wr_swing/result.json on the mini.
